about.story_text:
MoralEd was born from a shared belief: that character is the root of lifelong success. Inspired by both global research and local wisdom, we set out to build an educational ecosystem where values are not taught as extras—but lived as essentials.

From its earliest days, MoralEd has stood for more than curriculum. It has stood for culture. For community. For the timeless principles that shape not just students—but societies.
about.mission_lead: To nurture the whole child through culturally grounded, emotionally intelligent, and ethically driven education.
about.mission_body: We empower educators, families, and communities to raise children who lead with integrity and compassion. Our mission is not just to teach values—but to help children live them, feel them, and share them.
about.vision_text: A generation of young people who are not only academically capable, but emotionally aware, socially responsible, and morally courageous—ready to shape a more just and caring world.
about.framework_1_desc: We support academic, emotional, social, and moral growth in harmony.
about.framework_2_desc: Children engage with values through stories, choices, and reflection.
about.framework_3_desc: We build environments that reflect local identity and shared values.
about.framework_4_desc: We partner with families and communities to make character education real.
about.framework_5_desc: We track growth in empathy, responsibility, and ethical decision-making.
about.beliefs_text_1: Character is universal — it transcends borders, backgrounds, and beliefs, connecting us to our shared humanity. We believe education means more than knowledge: it means wisdom, empathy, and courage, lived in every classroom, not just taught in it.
about.timeline_2019_desc: MoralEd is founded with a vision to make character education central to every child's growth.
about.timeline_2020_desc: We launch our Whole Child Success Model, integrating emotional, ethical, and academic development.
about.timeline_2021_desc: Our first pilot schools begin implementing MoralEd values-based learning modules.
about.timeline_2023_desc: MoralEd expands across districts, adapting to local cultures and languages.

bullying.hero_subtitle: Character education works best alongside a clear, honest conversation about bullying — what it looks like, how to spot it, and what to do about it.
bullying.what_intro: Bullying is repeated, intentional behavior meant to hurt, intimidate, or exclude someone who has a hard time defending themselves. It can take several forms:
bullying.form_1_desc: Hitting, pushing, tripping, or damaging someone's belongings.
bullying.form_2_desc: Name-calling, teasing, threats, or insults repeated over time.
bullying.form_3_desc: Deliberate exclusion, spreading rumors, or damaging someone's relationships.
bullying.form_4_desc: Harassment, rumors, or exclusion carried out through phones, apps, or social media.
bullying.signs_title: Signs a Child May Be Experiencing Bullying
bullying.signs_intro: Every child is different, but these are common signs parents and teachers can watch for:
bullying.sign_1: Sudden reluctance to go to school or take part in activities they used to enjoy
bullying.sign_2: Unexplained cuts, bruises, or damaged belongings
bullying.sign_3: Changes in eating or sleeping habits
bullying.sign_4: Withdrawing from friends or family, or seeming anxious and low on confidence
bullying.sign_5: Asking for extra money or "losing" belongings often
bullying.tips_title: What to Do If You're Being Bullied
bullying.tip_1_desc: A friend, a parent, or a teacher — it is always okay to ask for help, and it is never your fault.
bullying.tip_2_desc: Bullying happens less often when you're with people who support you. Look for classmates who can back you up.
bullying.tip_3_desc: Stand tall, keep your voice steady, and say clearly that the behavior needs to stop. Then walk away and tell an adult.
bullying.tips_note: Every situation is different, and there's no single right answer — but keeping it to yourself is never the way through it.
bullying.family_text: If your child tells you about bullying, start by listening without judgment and thank them for telling you. Avoid promising to keep it secret, since adults at school may need to be involved to resolve it. Work with your child's teacher or school counselor on next steps, and check in regularly afterward — knowing someone is paying attention makes a real difference.
bullying.cta_text: Our monthly pillars — including Respect, Kindness, and Empathy — build the everyday habits that make bullying less likely to take root in the first place.

scopeSequence.title: Scope and Sequence
scopeSequence.intro: MoralEd follows a structured, month-by-month character education calendar. Each month introduces a core pillar, a set of related skills, and a clear learning objective your teachers can plan around and measure.
scopeSequence.skills_1: Kindness, compassion, empathy, helping others, mercy
scopeSequence.objective_1: By the end of September, students will practice acts of kindness and demonstrate empathy toward classmates.
scopeSequence.objective_2: By the end of October, students will complete tasks independently and take ownership of their actions.
scopeSequence.skills_3: Respect for self, others, teachers, parents, nature
scopeSequence.objective_3: By the end of November, students will communicate respectfully with peers, teachers, and family.
scopeSequence.objective_4: By the end of December, students will practice honesty and follow through on commitments.
scopeSequence.objective_5: By the end of January, students will apply fairness and inclusion in group activities and games.
scopeSequence.objective_6: By the end of February, students will take initiative in group projects and support teammates.
scopeSequence.objective_7: By the end of March, students will demonstrate resilience when facing academic or social challenges.
scopeSequence.objective_8: By the end of April, students will participate in a community or environmental service activity.
scopeSequence.objective_9: By the end of May, students will set and track progress toward a personal goal.

faq.hero_subtitle: Answers to the questions schools ask most before bringing MoralEd on board.
faq.question_1: What grade levels is MoralEd designed for?
faq.answer_1: MoralEd is built for K-12 classrooms, with activities, stories, and language adapted to fit different age groups within that range.
faq.question_2: How long does it take to bring MoralEd to our school?
faq.answer_2: Most schools move from an initial conversation to a classroom launch within a few weeks, depending on how much customization and teacher training your school needs. See our "Partner With Us" page for the full step-by-step process.
faq.question_3: Does MoralEd replace our existing curriculum?
faq.answer_3: No — MoralEd is designed to complement your existing curriculum, not replace it. The monthly pillar calendar fits alongside regular classroom instruction with dedicated activities, stories, and discussions.
faq.question_4: What languages is the program available in?
faq.answer_4: MoralEd is currently available in English, Russian, and Kyrgyz, so schools can deliver the program in the language that best fits their students and staff.
faq.question_5: What kind of training do our teachers need?
faq.answer_5: Before launch, your teachers receive hands-on training covering the curriculum structure, classroom activities, and how to track student progress each month. Ongoing support continues throughout the school year.
faq.question_6: How do we measure the program's impact?
faq.answer_6: We provide regular impact reports so you can see how students are progressing across each monthly pillar, based on teacher feedback and classroom observations.
faq.answer_7: Pricing depends on your school's size and the level of customization needed. Reach out through our contact page and our team will put together a quote tailored to your school.
faq.question_8: Can we customize the pillar calendar to fit our academic year?
faq.answer_8: Yes — during onboarding, we work with your school to align the 9-month pillar calendar with your specific academic year and any existing values or themes your school already emphasizes.
